title: 第23章 烬土西行第24章 火山部落的冲突
lines: 天算是亮了，可一点光都看不见。
铁城的早晨，是那种厚厚的、死气沉沉的白。云像块板子似的盖在天上，把太阳捂得严严实实，没有朝霞，没有暖色，连光影都糊成一片。整片大地都罩在一种均匀又冷冰冰的白光里，眼睛看到的一切都像褪了色，灰蒙蒙的，没一点活气。空气里堆着一股闷了一夜的土腥味和死水味儿，还混着辐射尘那种细细的焦糊气，吸进鼻子，喉咙就像堵了层砂纸，又涩又糙，怎么咳也咳不干净。每一次呼吸都又凉又沉，胸口像压着东西，闷得人心慌。
整座城看着倒是挺整齐，街道干净，哨岗林立，人来人往都守着规矩。表面是一片安稳，可那股冰冷的、细微的能量颗粒，始终飘在空气底下，顺着屋檐、街角、城墙外壁悄悄流动，无声无息的，摸着每一处可能没防备好的地方。
昨天这一整夜，铁城没人睡得着。
没有闹哄哄的动静，也没有交头接耳的议论，只有全城上下压着声音的忙活。铁手盟剩下的军官们通宵整理情报、调试武器、清点药品、查看西边荒原的路，所有动作又轻又快，一丝不乱，没一点多余的花样，只剩绝境临头时那种刻进骨子里的紧绷。
小院的木门推开了。
陆寻慢慢走出来，身体还带着透支后没缓过来的那种僵硬，背不算挺，肩膀看着松，底下却绷着一股僵硬的劲儿，那是长时间高压下，怎么也松不开的疲乏。眼睛还是一样灰暗，瞳孔缩得很小，对天亮没什么反应，看远处总像隔着一层擦不掉的灰雾，东西的轮廓老是模模糊糊的，带着重影。
胸口的十字徽章贴着皮肤，一整夜都在隐隐发烫，那感觉不尖锐，却钝钝地扎在肉里，让表面的皮肤一阵阵发麻发紧。它不声不响，却持续耗着体力，像有块看不见的石头压在胸口，逼得呼吸必须又轻又匀。左腿旧伤的酸胀也缠了一夜，现在脚一落地，骨头缝里就扯出一片细密的钝痛，整条腿又僵又沉，每走一步都显得有点吃力。这点破绽，被他靠着求生的本能死死压住，没露出来半分。
他穿着一身简单的作战服，袖口和衣摆都扎紧了，没有标记，也没有装饰，布料上沾着些细小的灰尘，是昨夜静坐时落下的。手指自然垂着，关节有点僵，手心一直冒着刺骨的寒意，血脉里还窜动着没平息的地脉乱流，皮肤表面发麻发木，身体的知觉像是隔了一层，又钝又模糊。
院子里的风停了。
光与影都凝固住，屋檐角的影子一动不动，整个空间陷入一片死寂。耳朵里嗡嗡作响，反而把远处极其细微的盔甲摩擦声、脚步声、武器归鞘的轻颤声，都放得清清楚楚。
林小满跟在他身后走出来。
她眉头一直紧皱着，皮肤绷得发白，没有半点放松。眼睛平视前方，眼皮微微垂着，眼底覆着一层浅灰的阴影，那是感知过度使用后一直没退去的痕迹。强迫自己休息了一整夜，精神上的刺痛却没减轻，反而因为一直绷着神经、不敢松懈，让疲惫一层层堆了起来。呼吸又浅又急，胸口起伏很轻，每一次试图舒展那些精神丝线，都会扯得脑袋深处又酸又麻。
她没整理头发，也没调整姿态，发丝就那么垂下来，遮住部分眉眼。脸上风干的泪痕还浅浅地印在皮肤里，冷风一吹，皮肤绷紧，泛起一阵生理性的寒意。从昨晚到现在，她的感知没有放松过一刻，始终维持着最外层的警戒，哪怕身心透支，也死死守在队伍最前面的这道感知防线上。
西边巷子尽头，一队人整齐地走近。
步伐均匀，起落一致，轻重相同，是铁手盟精锐老兵刻进骨子里的行军步调，冷硬规整，不带半点个人情绪。十个人，全都解下了武器垂着手，身板挺得笔直，肩膀和后背的肌肉绷得僵硬，眼里干干净净，只剩下绝对服从的克制。
领头的是个西线驻防的老兵，脸颊上布满了深深浅浅的灼伤疤痕，肤色是被火山热辐射和荒原辐射常年熏染成的暗红色，皮肤粗糙开裂，毛孔里嵌着洗不掉的火山灰。身上绕着淡淡的铁锈味、腐味和地热的焦糊气，那是五年在西线拉扯、常年死战留下的独有印记。
小队在院门外三米处齐刷刷停下。
动作整齐划一，没人出错，没人乱动，连呼吸都快调到同一个节奏。这种极致的规整，反而让整条死寂的巷子显得更加冰冷压抑。
老兵吐出一个字，声音粗粝沙哑，像被风沙磨过，没有起伏，没有情绪，纯粹是制式的汇报，“西行队伍准备完毕，急救药品、防辐射贴片、隔热装备、地形图，全部备齐。三匹耐跑的荒原驮马状态稳定，能全天赶路。”
“周盟主有令，西线所有驻防点临时开放，全力配合西行调度，沿途关卡一律放行，不阻拦、不盘问、不拖延。”
字字冰冷清楚，句句都落在实处，没有废话，只摆出最硬的准备事实。
陆寻抬眼，目光扫过这十人小队，看过他们绷紧的肩膀、布满伤疤的手、蓄势待发的姿态，眼里依旧灰暗，没有赞许，没有动容。
“出发。”
两个字落下，短促而锋利，切碎了清晨凝滞的死寂，瞬间把所有人的神经都拉紧了。
小队同时躬身领命，起身、转身，无声地回归队列，姿态依旧紧绷肃穆。
苏野最后从院里出来，一身作战服贴身利落，腰带束紧，武器固定得稳稳当当，身上没一点多余的东西。他眼睛死死盯着正西方向，瞳孔缩紧，所有注意力都锁在一个目标上。肩膀和后背的肌肉一直绷着，手臂线条拉直，全身都处在随时能爆发搏杀的戒备状态，没有松懈，只剩刻进骨子里的厮杀本能。
他没多余动作，也没多余眼神，只侧身站到队伍侧后方，默默接过了全程警戒的任务，目光扫过街道两侧、屋顶檐角、远处城墙的缺口，不留死角地排查着任何可能埋伏或异常的地方。
队伍开拔。
没有号角，没有口号，没有喧哗，只有整齐划一的脚步声，沉闷地砸在冰冷的青石板路上，在空旷死寂的街巷里荡开细碎的回音，又迅速被厚重的空气吞没，不留一点余响。
一路穿城而过，秩序森严。
街道两旁的岗哨笔直站着，眼神肃穆，没人张望，没人乱动，没人私语。所有守城的士兵都垂手肃立，用最标准的姿态目送队伍西行。铁城平定后的这种整齐，不是表面上的安稳，是无数从厮杀里活下来的人，用克制和敬畏沉淀出来的，是用硬实力压出来的绝对服从。
走到西城门。
厚重的合金城门完全敞开着，门洞又深又暗，隔开了城内死白的天光。门外，是无边无际的荒原灰雾，灰蒙蒙地铺在大地上，远近的景物糊成一片，边界都融化了，天地之间只剩下灰和白两种单调的颜色，视野被压得极窄，压抑感一下子翻了好几倍。
跨出门槛的一瞬间，风向变了。
冷风从西边荒原深处横刮过来，又尖又利，擦过耳朵，扫过皮肤，带着荒原独有的凛冽寒意，不是凉爽，是实实在在刺骨的冷，刮得露在外面的皮肤微微发麻发紧。空气里的味道也彻底变了，城里那股土腥味很快散去，取而代之的是浓烈的硫磺灼味、火山灰的干涩气，还有混在里面的、淡淡的辐射焦糊味。吸进肺里，又烫又糙，持续刺激着气管和鼻子，生理上的不适一层层往上叠。
城外的荒原，看不到一点活物的影子。
地面干裂板结，裂缝纵横交错，深不见底，缝里卡着经年堆积的死灰和板结的辐射尘垢，踩上去咯吱作响，声音干涩刺耳。远方的天际线完全模糊了，被一层厚厚的暗红色灰雾笼罩着——那是火山断裂带常年冒出来、散不去的火山尘雾，隔着几十里荒原都能看得清清楚楚，阴沉、压抑、死寂，明明白白预示着前路的凶险。
队伍出城后立刻提速，切换成了荒原赶路的节奏。
content_en:
It was daylight, but there was no light at all.
The morning in Tiecheng is that thick, lifeless white. The clouds cover the sky like a board, covering the sun tightly. There is no morning glow, no warm color, and even the light and shadow are blurred into one piece. The entire land was shrouded in a uniform and cold white light, and everything the eyes saw seemed faded, gray, and lifeless. The air was filled with the smell of earth and stagnant water that had been stifled all night, mixed with the fine burnt smell of radioactive dust. Inhaling into the nose, the throat felt like a layer of sandpaper was blocked, astringent and rough, and it could not be cleared no matter how hard I coughed. Every breath felt cold and heavy, and it felt like something was pressing on my chest, which made me panic.
The whole city looks quite neat, the streets are clean, there are many sentries, and everyone obeys the rules when coming and going. The surface is peaceful, but the cold, tiny energy particles are always floating in the air, flowing quietly along the eaves, street corners, and outer walls of the city walls, silently touching every place that may be unprepared.
All night yesterday, no one in Tiecheng could sleep.
There was no noisy movement, no whispering, just the busy business of the whole city with hushed voices. The remaining officers of the Iron Hand Alliance spent the whole night sorting out intelligence, debugging weapons, counting medicines, and checking the road to the western wasteland. All their actions were light and fast, without a trace of chaos, without any extraneous tricks, and only the tension that was engraved in their bones when a desperate situation approached.
The wooden door of the small courtyard was opened.
Lu Xun walked out slowly. His body was still stiff from overdraft. His back was not straight, and his shoulders looked loose, but there was a stiffness underneath. It was the fatigue that could not be relaxed after being under high pressure for a long time. His eyes are still as gray as ever, his pupils are very small, and he has no reaction to the dawn. When he sees a distance, it always seems like there is a layer of gray fog that cannot be wiped off, and the outlines of things are always blurry and have double images.
The cross badge on the chest was pressed against the skin, feeling faintly hot all night long. The feeling was not sharp, but it stabbed into the flesh bluntly, making the surface skin numb and tight. It was silent, but it continued to consume energy, like an invisible stone pressing on the chest, forcing the breath to be light and even. The old injury on my left leg had been sore and swollen all night, and now as soon as my foot landed, there was a fine, dull pain in the bones. The whole leg was stiff and heavy, and every step seemed a little laborious. This flaw was suppressed by his survival instinct, and it was not even exposed.
He was wearing a simple combat uniform, with the cuffs and hem tightly tied. There were no markings or decorations. The fabric was stained with fine dust that fell from the meditation last night. The fingers hang naturally, the joints are a bit stiff, the palms of the hands are always feeling bitingly cold, the unquenched earth veins are still flowing in the blood, the surface of the skin is numb, and the body's perception seems to be separated by a layer, dull and fuzzy.
The wind stopped in the yard.
Light and shadow were frozen, the shadows at the corners of the roof were motionless, and the entire space fell into dead silence. The ringing in his ears made the extremely subtle sounds of the scraping of armor, footsteps, and the slight tremble of weapons being sheathed in the distance clear.
Lin Xiaoman walked out behind him.
Her brows were frowning, her skin was tense and white, and she didn't relax at all. The eyes are looking straight ahead, the eyelids are slightly drooped, and there is a layer of light gray shadow under the eyes, which is the trace of overuse that has not receded. I forced myself to rest all night, but the mental sting did not lessen. On the contrary, because I kept tensing my nerves and did not dare to relax, my fatigue piled up layer by layer. His breathing was shallow and rapid, and his chest rose and fell very lightly. Every time he tried to stretch those mental threads, he would feel sore and numb in the depths of his head.
She didn't arrange her hair or adjust her posture. Her hair just hung down, covering part of her eyebrows. The dried tears on the face were still lightly imprinted on the skin. When the cold wind blew, the skin tightened and there was a physiological chill. From last night to now, her senses have not relaxed for a moment, and she has always maintained the outermost level of vigilance. Even if she is physically and mentally exhausted, she clings to the line of defense at the front of the team.
At the end of the west alley, a group of people approached neatly.
The pace is even, the rise and fall are consistent, and the weight is the same. It is the marching pace engraved in the bones of the elite veterans of the Iron Hand Alliance. It is cold and orderly, without any personal emotions. The ten people all took off their weapons and lowered their hands. Their bodies were straight, the muscles in their shoulders and backs were stiff, their eyes were clean, and only the restraint of absolute obedience remained.
The leader was a veteran garrisoned on the Western Front. His cheeks were covered with deep and shallow burn scars. His skin color was dark red that had been stained by volcanic heat radiation and wasteland radiation all year round. His skin was rough and cracked, and his pores were embedded with volcanic ash that could not be washed away. The body is surrounded by a faint smell of rust, rot and the burnt smell of geothermal heat, which are the unique marks left by five years of pulling and fighting on the Western Front and years of deadly fighting.
The team stopped in unison three meters outside the courtyard gate.
The movements were neat and uniform, no one made any mistakes, no one moved erratically, and even the breathing was quickly adjusted to the same rhythm. This extreme orderliness made the entire dead alley look even colder and more depressing.
"Report."
The veteran uttered one word. His voice was rough and hoarse, as if it had been worn by wind and sand. There were no ups and downs or emotions. It was purely a standard report. "The westbound team is ready. First aid medicines, radiation protection patches, heat insulation equipment, and terrain maps are all ready. The three durable wilderness draft horses are in stable condition and can travel all day."
"Leader Zhou has ordered that all garrison points on the western front be temporarily opened. We will fully cooperate with the dispatch of the westward journey. All checkpoints along the way will be allowed to pass without obstruction, questioning or delay."
The words are cold and clear, and every sentence is true to the point. There is no nonsense, only the most hard-to-prepare facts are presented.
Lu Xun raised his eyes and glanced at the ten-person team. He saw their tense shoulders, scarred hands, and ready postures. His eyes were still gray, without approval or emotion.
"Let's go."
The two words fell, short and sharp, cutting into pieces the dead silence of the early morning, and instantly tensed everyone's nerves.
The team bowed to accept the order at the same time, stood up, turned around, and silently returned to the queue, their postures still tense and solemn.
Su Ye finally came out of the courtyard, wearing a combat uniform that fit neatly on his body, his belt was tight, his weapons were securely fixed, and there was nothing extra on his body. His eyes were fixed on the west direction, his pupils were constricted, and all his attention was locked on one target. The muscles in the shoulders and back are always tense, the lines of the arms are straightened, and the whole body is in a state of alert that can break out into a fight at any time. There is no relaxation, only the fighting instinct engraved in the bones.
He made no extra moves or glances. He only stood sideways at the back of the team and silently took over the task of guarding the whole process. His eyes swept over both sides of the street, the corners of the roofs, and the gaps in the distant city wall, leaving no blind spots to investigate any possible ambush or abnormality.
The team sets off.
There were no horns, no slogans, no noises, only the sound of uniform footsteps, hitting the cold bluestone road dully, making tiny echoes in the empty and silent streets, and then quickly being swallowed up by the thick air, leaving no residual sound.
All the way through the city, order was strict.
The sentries on both sides of the street stood upright, with solemn eyes. No one looked, no one moved, no one whispered. All the soldiers guarding the city stood in silence with their hands lowered, watching the team march westward in the most standard manner. The neatness that Tiecheng had after it was pacified was not just the apparent stability, it was the result of the restraint and reverence of countless people who survived the fighting, and the absolute obedience exerted by hard power.
Walk to the west gate.
The thick alloy city gate was completely open. The door opening was deep and dark, blocking out the dead white skylight in the city. Outside the door, there is the endless gray fog of the wasteland, which is spread on the ground. The distant and near scenery are blurred into one, and the boundaries are melted. There are only two monotonous colors of gray and white left between the sky and the earth. The field of vision is extremely narrow, and the feeling of depression suddenly increases several times.
The moment he crossed the threshold, the wind direction changed.
The cold wind blew across from the depths of the wilderness to the west. It was sharp and sharp. It brushed against the ears and swept over the skin, bringing with it the unique biting chill of the wilderness. It was not cool, but a real biting cold. The exposed skin was slightly numb and tight. The smell in the air has also completely changed. The earthy smell in the city quickly dissipated, replaced by the strong smell of burning sulfur, the dry smell of volcanic ash, and the faint smell of burnt radiation mixed in. Inhaled into the lungs, it was hot and rough, continuously irritating the trachea and nose, and the physical discomfort piled up layer by layer.
In the wasteland outside the city, there was no sign of any living creature.
The ground is dry, cracked and hardened. The cracks are criss-crossed and bottomless. The cracks are filled with dead ash and hardened radiation dirt that have accumulated over the years. It creaks when you step on it, and the sound is dry and harsh. The distant skyline was completely blurred, shrouded in a thick layer of dark red gray mist - it was the volcanic dust mist that emerged from the volcanic fault zone all year round and could not be dissipated. It could be clearly seen across dozens of miles of wilderness. It was gloomy, oppressive, and dead, clearly indicating the danger of the road ahead.
After the team left the city, they immediately speeded up and switched to the rhythm of rushing through the wilderness.
title_en: Chapter 23: Embers Journey Westward Chapter 24: The Conflict of the Volcano Tribe
